newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Nov 11.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Russian novelist FEDOR DOSTOIEVSKI was born in 1821. He was initially sentenced to death for conspiracy against the Government but had his sentence commuted to life imprisonment in Siberia.
Works produced while in servitude included "Crime and Punishment", "The Idiot" and "The Brothers Karamazov".
The Frenchman whose name is now associated with a clinging vine LOUIS DE BOUGAINVILLE was born in 1829.
He commanded the first French circumnavigation of the world and as well as the vine an island in the Solomons group was named after him.
English lawyer BUTLER ASPINALL was born in 1830. He was the man who gained an acquittal for a Eureka Stockade rebel in Victoria.
The first QANTAS flight passenger ALEXANDER KENNEDY was born in 1837. The Australian grazier was issued Ticket number one for the inaugural flight from Longreach to Cloncurry in November 1922.
Australian artist ALICE BALE was born in 1875.
Australian jurist ELIZABETH EVATT was born in 1933.
American novelist KURT VONNEGUT, who was best known for "Slaughterhouse Five", was born in 1922.
Swedish actress BIBI ANDERSON, who appeared in INGMAR BERGMAN films, was born in 1935.
Norwegian keyboard player and songwriter with 'Europe' MIC MACHAELI was born in 1962.
** EVENTS **
1880 : Australia's most well known bushranger NED KELLY
was hanged at the Old Melbourne Jail. EDWARD 'NED' KELLY was born in Wallan in Victoria, the son of Irish convict RED KELLY and MARY QUINN.

NED began his life of crime relatively early and was jailed at the age of 16 for being in possession of a stolen horse. After his release NED and his gang set up a horse stealing ring and sold them over the border in New South Wales.
Other gang members were his brother DAN, JOE BYRNE and STEVE HART and sometimes MA KELLY also lent a hand with the "business".
The gang members had a base in the Wombat Ranges and eluded police for several months. A reward of 500 pounds was posted after NED shot and killed three police officers at Stringybark Creek.
That reward increased to 2000 pounds after they robbed a bank in Euroa and raided Jeridlerie. A raid at Glenrowan was the final siege.
1918 : After four years and 97 days the World War One
ended as the guns finally fell silent.
It was estimated more than nine million lives were lost, with another 27 million injured.
1920 : The bodies of the unknown British and French
soldiers were buired at Westminister Abbey and the Arc de Triomphe respectively.
1921 : The first Poppy Day was held to raise funds for
those wounded in World War One.
1923 : ADOLF HITLER was arrested after the failed Munich

beerhall putsch. The leader of the Bavarian National Socialist Party had invaded the city's largest beerhall with a large number of his armed Brownshirt guards. HITLER stood on a chair and fired a shot in the air and shouted "The National Revolution has begun". He fled after the man he linked arms with was shot.
1936 : Controversy surrounded a decision by Australia's
Minister of the Interior to stop a British woman from entering the country. The Minister Mr PATERSON denied Mrs FREER entery on the ground that she would have caused the "wreckage of an
Australian home".
It was believed that an Australian army officer was to leave his wife to marry Mrs FREER.
PATERSON was attacked in parliament for banning entry on "moral" grounds. Six months later Federal cabinet reversed the ban and the "scarlett woman" was allowed to land in Sydney.
1965 : The Rhodesian Front government declared Britain's
last African colony independent. The unilateral declaration by leader IAN SMITH underlined his opposition to sharing power with the black majority.
The British government imposed trade sanctions and an oil embargo. Northern Rhodesia became Zambia and Northern Rhodesia became Zimbabwe.
1975 : The Whitlam Labor government was sacked by the
Govenor-General. Parliament was dissolved and a provisional government commissioned.

The actions of Governor General Sir JOHN KERR followed weeks of politicial tension and a worsening constitutional crisis. After the Senate continually blocked supply Sir JOHN exercised his formerly unrecognised constitutional powers to dismiss the
government.
The opposition lead by MALCOLM FRASER had refused to pass the Budget Bill in the Senate ignoring a convention that the Senate should not reject budgets.
Mr FRASER was appointed prime minister and head of an interim government.
The shock dismissal prompted spontaneous demonstrations in Canberra and in other capital cities.
About two thousand people gathered around the steps of Parliament house chanting "We want Gough".
Mr WHITLAM addressed the supportive crowd and condemned the Governor-General's actions saying "Well may we say God savethe Queen because nothing will save the Governor-General".
In a reference to the appointed prime minister Mr WHITLAM called him "KERR's cur".
FRASER won the subsequent election.
1980 : QANTAS bomb hoaxer PETER MACARI was deported to
England after serving nine years of a 15-year sentence.
1981 : An armistice was signed between the inhabitants of
a Spanish village and Denmark after 172 years of conflict.
The long running disharmony began in 1809 when the leaders of the village of HUESCAR were disgruntled with Denmark siding with France against Britain in the Napoleonic Wars.
The Spanish village declared war on Denmark, but few knew about it. The peace was formally restored with the signing.
1987 : VAN GOGH's painting "Irises" was sold at Sotheby's
in New York for 53.9 million dollars.
1991 : MARTINA NAVRATILOVA equalled CHRIS EVERT's record
of 157 career titles when she defeated MONIKA SELES to win the Virgina Slims California Tournament in Oakland.
1994 : Telecom and RUPERT MURDOCH's News Limited formally
signed an agreement, becoming the first major player in future pay television services in Australia.
